Projects

Master's thesis, Riga Technical University, January 2026

Design and analysis of mechanical elements of a conveyor system

A 3D CAD model of a typical conveyor section (belt, rollers, frame and supports) for pharmaceutical logistics, built in ANSYS SpaceClaim and analyzed in ANSYS Workbench. The goal was to check structural behavior under 10, 20 and 30 N loads and to find the natural frequencies that matter for stable operation.

The model was meshed to about 2.77 million elements, with a grid independence study holding variation under 5%. Response stays linear and elastic across all three loads: stiffness holds near 25 N/mm, and peak von Mises stress reaches 7.31 MPa against a 250 MPa yield strength, a safety factor above 34.

A modal analysis extracted the first six natural frequencies for each load case. At 10 N they run from 4.3 Hz to 39.9 Hz.

ANSYS Workbench, ANSYS SpaceClaim, static structural analysis, modal analysis, grid independence study

Coursework, Riga Technical University

Technical system vibration and stability

Eight tasks that model vibrating systems from first principles and check them in software. Equations of motion were integrated numerically in Mathcad, and mechanisms and frames were simulated in SolidWorks Motion and SolidWorks Simulation.

Two results anchor the set: a single-degree-of-freedom response that peaks at an amplitude ratio of 36.5 at resonance, and a 500 mm steel tube frame whose first two modes both sit at 58.3 Hz.

Mathcad, SolidWorks Motion Analysis, SolidWorks frequency analysis

  • Opening-closing mechanism: equations of motion solved in Mathcad
  • Inverted pendulum: stable and unstable regimes in SolidWorks Motion
  • Amplitude response of a single-degree-of-freedom system
  • Resonance of a two-degree-of-freedom system
  • Natural frequency of a nonlinear system with geometric constraints
  • Wheel on a moving base over bumps and sharp-edged road
  • Pivoted beam with a spring, damper and hanging mass
  • Frequency analysis of a 500 mm steel tube frame

Automated scissor jack

Coursework

A motorized scissor jack that helps elderly and physically challenged users replace a tire. A 12V DC wiper motor turns rotary motion into reciprocating lifting motion, and the design centers on safety, less physical effort and reliability in extreme weather.

Q-Copter airflow simulation

SolidWorks Flow Simulation

Airflow around a quadcopter assembly placed in a rectangular flow domain. Pressure contours and flow trajectories show how air moves around the frame and its four rotors, and a velocity cut plot shows how speed varies around each rotor, up to 15 m/s.

CFD, pressure and velocity contours, flow trajectories

Airflow around a streamlined body

SolidWorks Flow Simulation

External flow over a teardrop-shaped body. Velocity contours on a cut plane peak near 39.6 m/s beside the rounded nose, velocity vectors trace the flow past the body, and a surface parameters table reports the pressure over the 0.149 m² surface.

CFD, external flow, velocity contours, surface pressure

Railway technical diagnostics

Coursework, experimental mechanics and technical diagnostics

A review of how railway transport is diagnosed and why maintenance is moving from fixed schedules to condition-based maintenance (CBM). It covers vibration analysis, infrared thermal monitoring, ultrasonic testing, oil analysis, laser wheel profiling and Motor Current Signature Analysis, with worked models for bearing defect frequencies and reliability.

In the worked example, a 14-roller axle bearing at 600 rpm produces an outer-race defect frequency of 60.15 Hz.

Condition-based maintenance, vibration analysis, thermal monitoring, reliability models
